sanskrit: tān pratyagṛhṇāt putras te madrarājaś ca vīryavān mahāmeghān iva bahūñ śailāv astodayāv ubhau
english: Your son and the valiant king of the Madras received those onrushing warriors, the two of them standing firm like the mountains of the eastern and western horizons confronting a host of great storm-clouds.

sanskrit: śalyas tu samaraślāghī dharmarājam ariṃdamam vavarṣa śaravarṣeṇa varṣeṇa maghavān iva
english: Śalya, glorying in battle, rained showers of arrows upon Yudhiṣṭhira, that tamer of foes, even as Maghavān pours down the rain.

sanskrit: tathaiva kururājo 'pi pragṛhya ruciraṃ dhanuḥ droṇopadeśān vividhān darśayāno mahāmanāḥ
english: In like manner the high-souled king of the Kurus too, taking up his splendid bow, displayed the manifold lessons taught him by Droṇa.

sanskrit: vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi citraṃ laghu ca suṣṭhu ca na cāsya vivaraṃ kaś cid dadarśa carato raṇe
english: He poured forth showers of arrows, wondrously, swiftly, and well; and as he ranged across the field of battle none could mark an opening in his guard.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau vividhair bāṇais tatakṣāte parasparam śārdūlāv āmiṣaprepsū parākrāntāv ivāhave
english: With their various shafts the two of them wounded each other, like two valiant tigers in combat, each greedy for the flesh of its prey.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu tava putreṇa raṇaśauṇḍena saṃgataḥ pāñcālyaḥ sātyakiś caiva mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau śakunipramukhān vīrān pratyagṛhṇan samantataḥ
english: Bhīma closed with your son, that drunkard of battle; and the prince of the Pāñcālas, and Sātyaki, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī received from every side the heroes led by Śakuni.

sanskrit: tadāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ punar eva jayaiṣiṇām tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca rājan durmantrite tava
english: Then once again, O king, fierce grew the battle between your men and the foe, both eager for victory—the fruit of your evil counsels.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu bhīmasya śareṇānataparvaṇā cicchedādiśya saṃgrāme dhvajaṃ hemavibhūṣitam
english: Duryodhana, taking deliberate aim, with a smooth-jointed arrow cut down in the fight Bhīma's banner adorned with gold.

sanskrit: sakiṅkiṇīkajālena mahatā cārudarśanaḥ papāta ruciraḥ siṃho bhīmasenasya nānadan
english: Fair to behold, with its great net of little bells, the splendid lion that was Bhīmasena's emblem fell roaring to the ground.

sanskrit: punaś cāsya dhanuś citraṃ gajarājakaropamam kṣureṇa śitadhāreṇa pracakarta narādhipaḥ
english: And again the king severed with a sharp-edged razor-shaft his brilliant bow, which was thick as the trunk of a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā tejasvī rathaśaktyā sutaṃ tava bibhedorasi vikramya sa rathopastha āviśat
english: His bow thus cut, the fiery Bhīma, advancing with a car-borne lance, pierced your son in the breast, and Duryodhana sank down upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: tasmin moham anuprāpte punar eva vṛkodaraḥ yantur eva śiraḥ kāyāt kṣurapreṇāharat tadā
english: While your son lay swooning, Vṛkodara then with a razor-headed shaft struck the head of his driver from his body.

sanskrit: hatasūtā hayās tasya ratham ādāya bhārata vyadravanta diśo rājan hāhākāras tadābhavat
english: Their charioteer slain, his horses, O Bhārata, bearing the car away, fled in all directions, O king, and a cry of dismay arose.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvat trāṇārthaṃ droṇaputro mahārathaḥ kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca putraṃ te 'bhiparīpsavaḥ
english: To his rescue rushed the mighty car-warrior, the son of Droṇa, and Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman, all bent on saving your son.

sanskrit: tasmin vilulite sainye trastās tasya padānugāḥ gāṇḍīvadhanvā visphārya dhanus tān ahanac charaiḥ
english: As that host was thrown into confusion, his foot-soldiers fled in terror; but the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, twanging his bow, struck them down with his shafts.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu madreśam abhyadhāvad amarṣitaḥ svayaṃ saṃcodayann aśvān dantavarṇān manojavān
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira, filled with wrath, charged upon the lord of the Madras, himself urging on his horses, ivory-white and swift as thought.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma kuntīputre yudhiṣṭhire purā bhūtvā mṛdur dānto yat tadā dāruṇo 'bhavat
english: There we beheld a marvel in Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira: he who before had been gentle and self-controlled had now grown terrible.

sanskrit: vivṛtākṣaś ca kaunteyo vepamānaś ca manyunā ciccheda yodhān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: With eyes wide open and trembling with fury, the son of Kuntī cut down warriors by hundreds of thousands with his whetted shafts.

sanskrit: yāṃ yāṃ pratyudyayau senāṃ tāṃ tāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa pāṇḍavaḥ śarair apātayad rājan girīn vajrair ivottamaiḥ
english: Whatever host advanced to meet him, that host the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas brought down with his arrows, O king, as great mountains are shattered by thunderbolts.

sanskrit: sāśvasūtadhvajarathān rathinaḥ pātayan bahūn ākrīḍad eko balavān pavanas toyadān iva
english: Felling many car-warriors with their horses, drivers, banners, and cars, the mighty one sported there alone, like the wind scattering the clouds.

sanskrit: sāśvārohāṃś ca turagān pattīṃś caiva sahasraśaḥ vyapothayata saṃgrāme kruddho rudraḥ paśūn iva
english: Horses with their riders, and foot-soldiers by the thousand, he crushed in the battle, as Rudra in his wrath crushes the beasts.

sanskrit: śūnyam āyodhanaṃ kṛtvā śaravarṣaiḥ samantataḥ abhyadravata madreśaṃ tiṣṭha śalyeti cābravīt
english: Having swept the field empty on every side with his showers of arrows, he charged upon the lord of the Madras and cried, "Stand, Śalya!"

sanskrit: tasya tac caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃgrāme bhīmakarmaṇaḥ vitresus tāvakāḥ sarve śalyas tv enaṃ samabhyayāt
english: Beholding this exploit of him whose deeds were dreadful in battle, all your men were seized with terror; but Śalya advanced to meet him.

sanskrit: tatas tau tu susaṃrabdhau pradhmāpya salilodbhavau samāhūya tadānyonyaṃ bhartsayantau samīyatuḥ
english: Then the two of them, swollen with fury, blew their conches born of the waters, and, challenging and defying one another, closed in combat.

sanskrit: śalyas tu śaravarṣeṇa yudhiṣṭhiram avākirat madrarājaṃ ca kaunteyaḥ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Śalya overwhelmed Yudhiṣṭhira with a shower of arrows, and the son of Kuntī in turn overwhelmed the king of the Madras with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: vyadṛśyetāṃ tadā rājan kaṅkapatribhir āhave udbhinnarudhirau śūrau madrarājayudhiṣṭhirau
english: Then, O king, the two heroes, the king of the Madras and Yudhiṣṭhira, were seen in the fight bristling with heron-feathered shafts, their blood gushing forth.

sanskrit: puṣpitāv iva rejāte vane śalmalikiṃśukā dīpyamānau mahātmānau prāṇayor yuddhadurmadau
english: The two high-souled warriors shone like a flowering śalmali and a kiṃśuka tree in the forest, ablaze with splendor, frenzied in their battle for life itself.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi sainyāni nādhyavasyaṃs tayor jayam hatvā madrādhipaṃ pārtho bhokṣyate 'dya vasuṃdharām
english: Beholding them, none of all the armies could foretell which of the two would win: "Once he has slain the lord of the Madras, Pārtha shall this day enjoy the earth;

sanskrit: śalyo vā pāṇḍavaṃ hatvā dadyād duryodhanāya gām itīva niścayo nābhūd yodhānāṃ tatra bhārata
english: "or else Śalya, having slain the Pāṇḍava, shall bestow the earth on Duryodhana"—thus, O Bhārata, no certainty came to the warriors there.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam abhūt sarvaṃ dharmarājasya yudhyataḥ
english: Yet for Yudhiṣṭhira, as he fought, every omen turned auspicious.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśataṃ śalyo mumocāśu yudhiṣṭhire dhanuś cāsya śitāgreṇa bāṇena nirakṛntata
english: Then Śalya swiftly loosed a hundred arrows at Yudhiṣṭhira, and with a sharp-pointed shaft he cut his bow asunder.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya śalyaṃ śaraśatais tribhiḥ avidhyat kārmukaṃ cāsya kṣureṇa nirakṛntata
english: Taking up another bow, Yudhiṣṭhira pierced Śalya with three hundred arrows and severed his bow with a razor-shaft.

sanskrit: athāsya nijaghānāśvāṃś caturo nataparvabhiḥ dvābhyām atha śitāgrābhyām ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then with smooth-jointed shafts he slew Śalya's four horses, and with two sharp-pointed ones the two drivers who guarded his flanks.

sanskrit: tato 'sya dīpyamānena pītena niśitena ca pramukhe vartamānasya bhallenāpāharad dhvajam tataḥ prabhagnaṃ tat sainyaṃ dauryodhanam ariṃdama
english: Then, as Śalya stood before him, with a blazing, golden, whetted broad-headed shaft he struck down his banner; and thereupon, O tamer of foes, that host of Duryodhana was broken.

sanskrit: tato madrādhipaṃ drauṇir abhyadhāvat tathākṛtam āropya cainaṃ svarathaṃ tvaramāṇaḥ pradudruve
english: Then the son of Droṇa rushed to the lord of the Madras, brought thus to such a pass, and lifting him into his own chariot bore him swiftly away.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tau gatvā nardamāne yudhiṣṭhire sthitvā tato madrapatir anyaṃ syandanam āsthitaḥ
english: Having gone but a little way, while Yudhiṣṭhira roared aloud, the lord of the Madras halted and mounted another chariot,

sanskrit: vidhivat kalpitaṃ śubhraṃ mahāmbudaninādinam sajjayantropakaraṇaṃ dviṣatāṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: a gleaming car duly equipped, that rumbled like a great rain-cloud, furnished with all its gear in readiness—a thing to make the foe's hair stand on end.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca athānyad dhanur ādāya balavad vegavattaram yudhiṣṭhiraṃ madrapatir viddhvā siṃha ivānadat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, taking up another bow, mightier and swifter still, the lord of the Madras pierced Yudhiṣṭhira and roared like a lion.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śaravarṣeṇa parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān abhyavarṣad ameyātmā kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: Then that bull among warriors, immeasurable of soul, rained down a shower of arrows upon the kṣatriyas, like Parjanya pouring forth the rain.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ daśabhir viddhvā bhīmasenaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ sahadevaṃ tribhir viddhvā yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: Piercing Sātyaki with ten shafts, Bhīmasena with three, and Sahadeva with three, he then pressed hard upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tāṃs tān anyān maheṣvāsān sāśvān sarathakuñjarān kuñjarān kuñjarārohān aśvān aśvaprayāyinaḥ rathāṃś ca rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ jaghāna rathināṃ varaḥ
english: That foremost of car-warriors slew sundry other mighty bowmen together with their horses, chariots, and elephants—elephants with their riders, horses with their cavalrymen, and chariots together with their warriors.

sanskrit: bāhūṃś ciccheda ca tathā sāyudhān ketanāni ca cakāra ca mahīṃ yodhais tīrṇāṃ vedīṃ kuśair iva
english: He severed arms still grasping their weapons, and banners as well, and made the earth thickly strewn with warriors as an altar is strewn with kuśa grass.

sanskrit: tathā tam arisainyāni ghnantaṃ mṛtyum ivāntakam parivavrur bhṛśaṃ kruddhāḥ pāṇḍupāñcālasomakāḥ
english: As he slaughtered the hostile hosts like Death the all-ender himself, the Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas, and Somakas, exceedingly enraged, surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaś ca śineś ca naptā; mādryāś ca putrau puruṣapravīrau samāgataṃ bhīmabalena rājñā; paryāpur anyonyam athāhvayantaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, and the grandson of Śini, and the two sons of Mādrī, foremost of men, came upon him as he closed with their king of dreadful might; and, calling upon one another, they hemmed him in.

sanskrit: tatas tu śūrāḥ samare narendraṃ; madreśvaraṃ prāpya yudhāṃ variṣṭham āvārya cainaṃ samare nṛvīrā; jaghnuḥ śaraiḥ patribhir ugravegaiḥ
english: Then those heroes, having reached that king, the lord of the Madras, best of fighters, and having hemmed him about in the battle, those manly warriors struck him with feathered shafts of terrible speed.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣito bhīmasenena rājā; mādrīsutābhyām atha mādhavena madrādhipaṃ patribhir ugravegaiḥ; stanāntare dharmasuto nijaghne
english: Guarded by Bhīmasena, by the two sons of Mādrī, and by Mādhava, the son of Dharma struck the lord of the Madras between the breasts with feathered shafts of terrible speed.

sanskrit: tato raṇe tāvakānāṃ rathaughāḥ; samīkṣya madrādhipatiṃ śarārtam paryāvavruḥ pravarāḥ sarvaśaś ca; duryodhanasyānumate samantāt
english: Then in the battle the throngs of your car-warriors, the foremost among them, seeing the lord of the Madras sore beset with arrows, surrounded him on all sides, with Duryodhana's consent.

sanskrit: tato drutaṃ madrajanādhipo raṇe; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ saptabhir abhyavidhyat taṃ cāpi pārtho navabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; vivyādha rājaṃs tumule mahātmā
english: Then swiftly the king of the Madra folk pierced Yudhiṣṭhira in the fight with seven shafts; and the high-souled Pārtha in turn pierced him with nine arrows, O king, amid that tumult.

sanskrit: ākarṇapūrṇāyatasaṃprayuktaiḥ; śarais tadā saṃyati tailadhautaiḥ anyonyam ācchādayatāṃ mahārathau; madrādhipaś cāpi yudhiṣṭhiraś ca
english: With arrows drawn back to the ear, oil-washed and well-aimed, the two great car-warriors—the lord of the Madras and Yudhiṣṭhira—then veiled each other from sight in the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tu tūrṇaṃ samare mahārathau; parasparasyāntaram īkṣamāṇau śarair bhṛśaṃ vivyadhatur nṛpottamau; mahābalau śatrubhir apradhṛṣyau
english: Then swiftly those two great car-warriors, those best of kings, mighty in strength and unassailable by their foes, watching for each other's opening, pierced one another sorely with their shafts.

sanskrit: tayor dhanurjyātalanisvano mahān; mahendravajrāśanitulyanisvanaḥ parasparaṃ bāṇagaṇair mahātmanoḥ; pravarṣator madrapapāṇḍuvīrayoḥ
english: As those two high-souled heroes, the Madra warrior and the son of Pāṇḍu, rained masses of arrows upon each other, the great twang of their bowstrings against their wrist-guards rang out like the crash of great Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tau ceratur vyāghraśiśuprakāśau; mahāvaneṣv āmiṣagṛddhināv iva viṣāṇinau nāgavarāv ivobhau; tatakṣatuḥ saṃyugajātadarpau
english: The two ranged the field, bright as tiger-cubs greedy for flesh in the great forest, and like two tusked lordly elephants they gashed each other, their pride born of the combat.

sanskrit: tatas tu madrādhipatir mahātmā; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhīmabalaṃ prasahya vivyādha vīraṃ hṛdaye 'tivegaṃ; śareṇa sūryāgnisamaprabheṇa
english: Then the high-souled lord of the Madras, overpowering Yudhiṣṭhira of terrible might, pierced that hero with great force in the heart, with a shaft bright as the sun and as fire.

sanskrit: tato 'tividdho 'tha yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi; susaṃprayuktena śareṇa rājan jaghāna madrādhipatiṃ mahātmā; mudaṃ ca lebhe ṛṣabhaḥ kurūṇām
english: Then, sorely wounded, the high-souled Yudhiṣṭhira too, O king, struck the lord of the Madras with a well-aimed shaft, and that bull of the Kurus took joy thereat.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād iva pārthivendro; labdhvā saṃjñāṃ krodhasaṃraktanetraḥ śatena pārthaṃ tvarito jaghāna; sahasranetrapratimaprabhāvaḥ
english: Then, after a moment, that lord of kings, recovering his senses, his eyes red with wrath, his might like that of the thousand-eyed one, swiftly struck Pārtha with a hundred shafts.

sanskrit: tvaraṃs tato dharmasuto mahātmā; śalyasya kruddho navabhiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ bhittvā hy uras tapanīyaṃ ca varma; jaghāna ṣaḍbhis tv aparaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ
english: Then the high-souled son of Dharma in haste and wrath, with nine shafts piercing Śalya's breast and his golden mail, smote him again with six other arrows.

sanskrit: tatas tu madrādhipatiḥ prahṛṣṭo; dhanur vikṛṣya vyasṛjat pṛṣatkān dvābhyāṃ kṣurābhyāṃ ca tathaiva rājñaś; ciccheda cāpaṃ kurupuṃgavasya
english: Then the lord of the Madras, full of joy, drawing his bow, let fly his shafts, and with two razor-headed arrows cut the bow of the king, that bull among the Kurus.

sanskrit: navaṃ tato 'nyat samare pragṛhya; rājā dhanur ghorataraṃ mahātmā śalyaṃ tu viddhvā niśitaiḥ samantād; yathā mahendro namuciṃ śitāgraiḥ
english: Then in the battle the high-souled king, taking up another bow, yet more terrible, pierced Śalya on every side with whetted shafts, as great Indra pierced Namuci with his sharp-pointed bolts.

sanskrit: tatas tu śalyo navabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; bhīmasya rājñaś ca yudhiṣṭhirasya nikṛtya raukme paṭuvarmaṇī tayor; vidārayām āsa bhujau mahātmā
english: Then the high-souled Śalya, with nine shafts, having cut through the stout golden corslets of both Bhīma and king Yudhiṣṭhira, tore open their arms.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa jvalitārkatejasā; kṣureṇa rājño dhanur unmamātha kṛpaś ca tasyaiva jaghāna sūtaṃ; ṣaḍbhiḥ śaraiḥ so 'bhimukhaṃ papāta
english: Then with another razor-shaft, blazing with the sun's splendor, he shattered the king's bow; and Kṛpa with six arrows slew the king's charioteer, who fell forward upon his face.

sanskrit: madrādhipaś cāpi yudhiṣṭhirasya; śaraiś caturbhir nijaghāna vāhān vāhāṃś ca hatvā vyakaron mahātmā; yodhakṣayaṃ dharmasutasya rājñaḥ
english: And the lord of the Madras with four arrows slew the horses of Yudhiṣṭhira; and having slain them, that high-souled one wrought havoc among the warriors of king Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: tathā kṛte rājani bhīmaseno; madrādhipasyāśu tato mahātmā chittvā dhanur vegavatā śareṇa; dvābhyām avidhyat subhṛśaṃ narendram
english: When the king was thus served, the high-souled Bhīmasena swiftly cut the bow of the lord of the Madras with a fast-flying shaft and pierced that king sorely with two arrows.

sanskrit: athāpareṇāsya jahāra yantuḥ; kāyāc chiraḥ saṃnahanīyamadhyāt jaghāna cāśvāṃś caturaḥ sa śīghraṃ; tathā bhṛśaṃ kupito bhīmasenaḥ
english: Then with another shaft he struck the head of his driver from his body, from the midst of his armor; and the sorely enraged Bhīmasena swiftly slew his four horses as well.

sanskrit: tam agraṇīḥ sarvadhanurdharāṇām; ekaṃ carantaṃ samare 'tivegam bhīmaḥ śatena vyakirac charāṇāṃ; mādrīputraḥ sahadevas tathaiva
english: As that foremost of all bowmen ranged the battle alone with great swiftness, Bhīma covered him with a hundred arrows, and so too did Sahadeva, the son of Mādrī.

sanskrit: taiḥ sāyakair mohitaṃ vīkṣya śalyaṃ; bhīmaḥ śarair asya cakarta varma sa bhīmasenena nikṛttavarmā; madrādhipaś carma sahasratāram
english: Seeing Śalya dazed by those shafts, Bhīma with his arrows cut through his armor; and his corslet thus rent by Bhīmasena, the lord of the Madras seized a shield set with a thousand stars.

sanskrit: pragṛhya khaḍgaṃ ca rathān mahātmā; praskandya kuntīsutam abhyadhāvat chittvā ratheṣāṃ nakulasya so 'tha; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhīmabalo 'bhyadhāvat
english: And taking up a sword, the high-souled one leapt down from his chariot and rushed upon the son of Kuntī; having cut the chariot-pole of Nakula, that one of dreadful might bore down upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi rājānam athotpatantaṃ; kruddhaṃ yathaivāntakam āpatantam dhṛṣṭadyumno draupadeyāḥ śikhaṇḍī; śineś ca naptā sahasā parīyuḥ
english: And as that king sprang forward, wrathful, swooping like Death the all-ender, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the sons of Draupadī, Śikhaṇḍin, and the grandson of Śini suddenly surrounded him.

sanskrit: athāsya carmāpratimaṃ nyakṛntad; bhīmo mahātmā daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkaḥ khaḍgaṃ ca bhallair nicakarta muṣṭau; nadan prahṛṣṭas tava sainyamadhye
english: Then the high-souled Bhīma cut his peerless shield to pieces with ten shafts, and with broad-headed arrows severed his sword at the hilt, roaring with joy in the midst of your host.

sanskrit: tat karma bhīmasya samīkṣya hṛṣṭās; te pāṇḍavānāṃ pravarā rathaughāḥ nādaṃ ca cakrur bhṛśam utsmayantaḥ; śaṅkhāṃś ca dadhmuḥ śaśisaṃnikāśān
english: Beholding that deed of Bhīma, the foremost throngs of the Pāṇḍavas' car-warriors, rejoicing, raised a mighty shout, laughing aloud, and blew their conches white as the moon.

sanskrit: tenātha śabdena vibhīṣaṇena; tavābhitaptaṃ balam aprahṛṣṭam svedābhibhūtaṃ rudhirokṣitāṅgaṃ; visaṃjñakalpaṃ ca tathā viṣaṇṇam
english: At that terrible din your army was sore afflicted and joyless, overcome with sweat, its limbs drenched in blood, half-senseless and downcast.

sanskrit: sa madrarājaḥ sahasāvakīrṇo; bhīmāgragaiḥ pāṇḍavayodhamukhyaiḥ yudhiṣṭhirasyābhimukhaṃ javena; siṃho yathā mṛgahetoḥ prayātaḥ
english: That king of the Madras, suddenly hemmed in by the chief Pāṇḍava warriors led by Bhīma, sped swiftly straight toward Yudhiṣṭhira, as a lion makes for its prey.

sanskrit: sa dharmarājo nihatāśvasūtaṃ; krodhena dīptajvalanaprakāśam dṛṣṭvā tu madrādhipatiṃ sa tūrṇaṃ; samabhyadhāvat tam ariṃ balena
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira, beholding the lord of the Madras, his horses and driver slain, blazing with wrath like a kindled fire, swiftly rushed upon that foe with all his might.

sanskrit: govindavākyaṃ tvaritaṃ vicintya; dadhre matiṃ śalyavināśanāya sa dharmarājo nihatāśvasūte; rathe tiṣṭhañ śaktim evābhikāṅkṣan
english: Calling swiftly to mind the words of Govinda, he set his heart upon the slaying of Śalya; and Yudhiṣṭhira, standing in his chariot whose horses and driver were slain, longed for his spear.

sanskrit: tac cāpi śalyasya niśamya karma; mahātmano bhāgam athāvaśiṣṭam smṛtvā manaḥ śalyavadhe yatātmā; yathoktam indrāvarajasya cakre
english: And, marking that deed of the high-souled Śalya, and remembering the portion of doom that yet remained for him, the self-controlled king bent his mind upon Śalya's slaying, even as Viṣṇu, the younger brother of Indra, had bidden him.

sanskrit: sa dharmarājo maṇihemadaṇḍāṃ; jagrāha śaktiṃ kanakaprakāśām netre ca dīpte sahasā vivṛtya; madrādhipaṃ kruddhamanā niraikṣat
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira seized a spear, golden of sheen, its shaft set with gems and gold; and opening wide his blazing eyes, with mind enraged he gazed upon the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: nirīkṣito vai naradeva rājñā; pūtātmanā nirhṛtakalmaṣeṇa abhūn na yad bhasmasān madrarājas; tad adbhutaṃ me pratibhāti rājan
english: Gazed upon, O king of men, by that pure-souled monarch whose sins were purged away, that the king of the Madras was not reduced to ashes—this seems to me a marvel, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tu śaktiṃ rucirogradaṇḍāṃ; maṇipravālojjvalitāṃ pradīptām cikṣepa vegāt subhṛśaṃ mahātmā; madrādhipāya pravaraḥ kurūṇām
english: Then that high-souled and foremost of the Kurus hurled with great force and swiftness at the lord of the Madras the blazing spear, its splendid fierce shaft alight with gems and coral.

sanskrit: dīptām athaināṃ mahatā balena; savisphuliṅgāṃ sahasā patantīm praikṣanta sarve kuravaḥ sametā; yathā yugānte mahatīm ivolkām
english: As it sped down blazing, hurled with mighty strength, scattering sparks, all the assembled Kurus gazed upon it as upon a great meteor at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: tāṃ kālarātrīm iva pāśahastāṃ; yamasya dhātrīm iva cograrūpām sabrahmadaṇḍapratimām amoghāṃ; sasarja yatto yudhi dharmarājaḥ
english: That spear, like the Night of Doom with her noose in hand, like the dread nurse of Yama, terrible of aspect, unfailing, the very likeness of Brahmā's rod, Yudhiṣṭhira, intent, let fly in the battle.

sanskrit: gandhasrag agryāsanapānabhojanair; abhyarcitāṃ pāṇḍusutaiḥ prayatnāt saṃvartakāgnipratimāṃ jvalantīṃ; kṛtyām atharvāṅgirasīm ivogrām
english: That spear, worshipped with diligence by the sons of Pāṇḍu with perfumes and garlands, with the choicest seats, drink, and food, blazed like the fire of universal dissolution, terrible as a destroying spell of the Atharvan and Aṅgiras seers.
